FINDING 0b — a full C-vs-JS differential over the REAL corpus
(tests/fixtures/zen/*.zen + examples/*.zen, 241 programs) found FOUR programs
where both backends exit 0 and print different things. Totals:

    AGREE=80  DIVERGENCE=4  JS-RUNTIME-FAIL=63  JS-UNSUPPORTED=0  C-FAIL=94

(C-FAIL = the program is a deliberate reject fixture or needs argv/stdin, so it
never got to the JS side; those are skipped, not failures.)

THE FOUR DIVERGENCES — every command below is `./zen run <f>` versus
`./zen emit-js <f> | node`:

  1. tests/fixtures/zen/generic_literal_pin.zen
       C : 8 8 8 8 4 8 4 1 255
       JS: 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 255
       -> sizeof is hard-coded 8 in the JS runtime. Minimal repro and full
          write-up: js_sizeof_always_8.{zen.txt,NOTES.txt}

  2. tests/fixtures/zen/inliner_eval_once.zen
       C : count=3 / v=6 / done
       JS: count=0 / v=6 / done
       -> a `store` through an `addr()` never reaches the variable on JS.

  3. tests/fixtures/zen/raw_intrinsics_at.zen
       C : 42          (x := 41; p := @addr(x); println(@load(p) + 1))
       JS: 1
       -> same cause: `@load` through an `addr()` reads 0.

  4. examples/strings_demo.zen
       C : "parsed 3 of 4 lines; column widths 19/5/5/15" + a rendered table
       JS: "parsed 0 of 4 lines; column widths 0/0/0/0"  + an empty table
       -> byte-level string scanning over the JS linear memory is wrong.

MINIMAL REPRO for 2 and 3 — js_addr_is_identity_divergence.zen.txt:
        c: i32 := 0
        p := c.addr()
        store(p, 7)
        println(c)          # C: 7   JS: 0     <-- divergence
        println(load(p))    # C: 7   JS: 7
CMD:  ./zen run     tests/fixtures/zen/fuzz-repro/js_addr_is_identity_divergence.zen.txt
      ./zen emit-js tests/fixtures/zen/fuzz-repro/js_addr_is_identity_divergence.zen.txt | node
ROOT: bootstrap/zenrt.js:56  `const addr = (x) => x;` — "JS objects are
      references; scalar aliasing is DEFERRED (boxed refs)". `c.addr()` yields
      the VALUE, so `store` writes to a copy and the original never changes.

THE STRUCTURAL POINT: JS-UNSUPPORTED was 0 over the whole corpus. `emit-js`
never refuses anything. Both of the runtime's deferred stubs (addr, sizeof) are
deferred as WRONG ANSWERS rather than as refusals, so a Zen program that the
compiler happily emits for the JS target can print different numbers than the
same program under C, with no warning at either compile or run time. That is
the difference between "known feature gap" and "silent miscompile".

CLASS: miscompile (C/JS divergence, both exit 0).
